# Highest points of European countries — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/highest-points-of-europe.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/highest-points-of-europe.ttl`](../decks/highest-points-of-europe.ttl) · **Cards:** 40 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

The highest point of 40 sovereign states of Europe, one card each: the states that the UN's M49 standard places in Europe, Russia included and Cyprus, Turkey and the Caucasus states not, leaving out Italy, Serbia, Monaco and Vatican City, whose highest point is disputed or not a named summit. Front: the country, e.g. “Highest point of Sweden”; back: the name of the summit in English and Swedish, often with a short note. For Denmark the card asks about Denmark proper (without Greenland and the Faroe Islands), for the Netherlands about the European part. Taken from Wikidata and checked against the CIA World Factbook's last edition, Wikipedia and national sources.

## Licensing

The only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: which summit is each state's highest point, the English and Swedish names of the summits and states and the alternative names in the notes come from it, so the deck is CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. Every other source was used for verification only: the CIA World Factbook (public domain, but not needed as content), the English and Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0), the UN M49 page (UN terms of use, non-commercial), Stockholm University, STATEC and Lex (all rights reserved or no open licence). They confirmed facts, and no wording or table was copied from them; the fronts and notes are the compiler's own wording of facts. The one thing a verification source decided is which states get a card: the deck follows the UN M49 standard's region Europe. M49 is a classification that assigns every country or area of the world to one region; that a state belongs to its region Europe is a fact of the standard, as an ISO code is, and facts are not protected by copyright, so using them to decide the deck's scope copies nothing protected. No list was taken over: the deck's items are the states with their Wikidata highest points, with exclusions decided and explained here, and the English Wikipedia list's own selection, which differs, was not used.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. 1. Wikidata (query 1): every item that is a sovereign state (P31 Q3624078) on the continent Europe (P30 Q46), apart from states with limited recognition (P31 Q3024240), with its M49 code (P2082), every P610 (highest point) statement with its rank, the English, Swedish and mul labels of the point and its elevation (P2044). The result has 49 items, among them the transcontinental Russia, Turkey, Georgia and Kazakhstan and Cyprus (Armenia and Azerbaijan are not on the continent Europe in Wikidata), but neither Denmark (Q35) nor the Netherlands (Q55), whose items are constituent countries; their P610 statements were fetched with query 2. Query 1 also returned the items Kingdom of Denmark and Kingdom of the Netherlands and, despite the filter, Kosovo; none of the three is a card.
3. 2. Selection: the states were limited to those that the UN Statistics Division's M49 standard places in its region Europe (code 150), parsed from the M49 overview page (query 5, script m49.py: the rows of the page's first, English table whose third cell, Region Code, is "150"): 51 rows, of which 44 are sovereign states (43 UN members and the Holy See) and 7 are dependencies (Åland, the Faroe Islands, Guernsey, the Isle of Man, Jersey, Svalbard and Jan Mayen, Gibraltar). So M49 decides which states get a card (see Licensing for why that is a fact that may be used). An attempt to corroborate the region membership from Wikidata (query 16: states that are part of (P361) the items with the M49 codes 154, 151, 039 and 155) returned no rows, because Wikidata does not link the states to those items. M49 puts Russia in Eastern Europe, and Cyprus, Turkey, Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan in Western Asia and Kazakhstan in Central Asia, so those six are not in the deck, and Russia's card asks for the highest point of Russia as a whole (Mount Elbrus, in the Caucasus). Four of the 44 were then left out (see Selection): Italy, Serbia, Monaco and Vatican City. 40 cards.
4. 3. Independent check, all states: The World Factbook of the CIA, discontinued in February 2026, was read in its last edition from the public-domain factbook.json repository (query 6; country files last updated 22 January 2026), field Geography > Elevation > highest point. Further check: the English Wikipedia's "List of highest points of European countries" (revision 1374673390), fetched as wikitext through the MediaWiki API and parsed by enwiki_parse.py (query 7). Every card's summit was compared with both by reading the three readings side by side; the differences are listed under quality control (round 0).
5. 4. National and other sources where the readings differed or a fact changes: for Sweden the Tarfala research station's 2026 measurement of Kebnekaise (11 September 2026) as published by Stockholm University on 16 September 2026 (query 9; the dossier first cited the 2025 measurement, see quality-control round 1); for Luxembourg the national statistics office's "Luxembourg in figures 2025" (query 10) and the English Wikipedia article Kneiff (query 8); for Denmark the Lex (Den Store Danske) article Møllehøj (query 11). The brief named Lantmäteriet; Stockholm University's Tarfala station makes the annual measurement of the Kebnekaise peaks, so its report was used instead.
6. 5. Names: the English back is the Wikidata English label of the summit, except for Belarus, where the English label "Dziaržynkaja hara" is a Belarusian Latin form that no other source uses: the card uses the English alias "Dzyarzhynskaya Hara" (also the Factbook's and the English Wikipedia's form). The Swedish back is the Wikidata Swedish label where it equals the title of the Swedish Wikipedia article (sitelink, query 3) and the local official form; otherwise: Ireland "Carrauntoohil" (the Irish official form and a Swedish alias; the Swedish label is "Carrauntoohill" and the Swedish article "Carrantuohill"), Finland "Haldefjäll" (the Swedish Wikipedia title and Finland-Swedish name, also an English alias; the Swedish label writes "Halde fjäll"; changed from "Halti" in quality-control round 2), Malta "Ta' Dmejrek" (the mul label, with the Maltese apostrophe and space; the Swedish label is "Ta'Dmejrek"), Croatia "Dinara" (the mul label; there is no Swedish label or article). Where Swedish and English differ the Swedish form is the one in Swedish use (Olympos, Elbrus, Moldoveanu, Aukštojas, Dealul Bălănești, Ponta do Pico, Hvannadalshnjúkur, Gora Dzerzjinskaja). Liechtenstein's card says "Vorder-Grauspitz" in both languages (the Swedish label and article, the Factbook and the English list; the English label is "Grauspitz"), so the answer does not depend on the language (quality-control round 2). Country names are the Wikidata English and Swedish labels, with "Czechia" (the short name the UN uses, an English alias) for the Czech Republic. Swedish fronts read "Högsta punkten i <land>", which avoids genitives of names such as Schweiz, except for the island states, where Swedish says "på": "Högsta punkten på Island" and "Högsta punkten på Malta". English fronts read "Highest point of <country>", with the article where English uses one ("the United Kingdom", "the European Netherlands").
7. 6. Swedish check: the introductions of the Swedish Wikipedia articles were fetched through the MediaWiki API with their revision ids (query 4, svwiki.py); the evidence quotes the sentences of the introduction (split at ". ") that contain a keyword chosen per card: "högsta" for most cards ("högst" for Iceland), plus or instead: Andorra "Coma Pedrosa är", Belgium "ås", Bosnia and Herzegovina "gränsen" and "Veliki", Czechia "Tjeckiens" and "gränsen", Finland "Finlands" and "Norge", France "Alpernas", Germany "Österrike", the Netherlands "trelandsgränspunkt", Poland "gränsen" and "Slovakien", Romania "Făgăraș", Russia "Elbrus (" and "Europas", Slovakia "Karpaterna", Spain "Spaniens" and "Teneriffa", Sweden "Nordtoppen", Switzerland "Monte Rosa", Ukraine "Hoverla (" and the United Kingdom "Skottland"; if none matched, the first sentence (Zla Kolata, whose introduction does not call it Montenegro's highest point). Dinara has no Swedish article. Germany's sentence on the Bavarian Alps was added to the evidence by hand in quality-control round 3.
8. 7. Cards: front "Highest point of <country>" / "Högsta punkten i <land>" ("på" for Iceland and Malta); back: the summit; backNote: short context (mountain range, border, the mainland high point of Spain and Portugal, other names), every fact of it from one of the sources named in the card's evidence. Elevations are left off the cards because surveys differ; the one exception is Kebnekaise's north peak, given with its source and year because the change of Sweden's highest point is the point of the note. Denmark and the Netherlands are asked about their European part: Denmark proper (front note), whose highest point is Møllehøj (the Kingdom of Denmark's is Gunnbjørn Fjeld in Greenland), and the European Netherlands, whose highest point is the Vaalserberg (the whole country's is Mount Scenery on Saba). Study direction front to back, because Korab answers two cards (Albania and North Macedonia).
9. 8. The dossier was generated from the saved query results by make_dossier.py, which writes each card's evidence from the parsed readings (the Wikidata statements and labels, the Factbook text, the English Wikipedia row, the Swedish Wikipedia sentence); the Stockholm University, STATEC, Kneiff and Lex readings were added by hand from the fetched pages, and the changes of quality-control rounds 1–3 were made by hand from the readings of queries 9 and 13–16. The scripts are not published with the deck; the steps above give what they do, including the parsing rule of m49.py (step 2) and the keywords of svwiki.py's sentence choice (step 6).
10. 9. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata that the country item has the summit as a P610 value, that the summit has the English and Swedish back as a label or alias (in that language or mul), and that the country item has the English and Swedish country name of the front. For the Netherlands the builder's P610 check cannot be used: it reads only best-rank values, and the Vaalserberg is a normal-rank P610 value of Q55 beside the preferred Mount Scenery (query 2), so the card checks instead that the Vaalserberg's country (P17) is the Netherlands. That is only a sanity check (the Vaalserberg also has Belgium and Germany as P17 values); the real Wikidata support for the card is the normal-rank P610 value of Q55 read with query 2. Two label checks are left out on purpose: Finland's Swedish back "Haldefjäll" is the Swedish Wikipedia sitelink of Q216035 but not a Swedish label or alias (the label is "Halde fjäll"), and Liechtenstein's English back "Vorder-Grauspitz" is not an English label or alias of Q665000 (the label is "Grauspitz"); both are documented in the cards' evidence. The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (validate_sources.ts).

## Selection

The sovereign states that the UN M49 standard places in Europe (43 UN members and the Holy See), as of 4 October 2026, each with its highest point: 40 cards. Transcontinental states follow M49: Russia is in (its highest point is Mount Elbrus in the Caucasus, the highest point of Russia as a whole), while Turkey, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Cyprus (Western Asia) and Kazakhstan (Central Asia) are out; so are Kosovo (not a UN member and not listed by M49) and the dependencies (Åland, the Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Guernsey, the Isle of Man, Jersey, Svalbard and Jan Mayen). Left out of the 44: Italy, because sources differ on whether its highest point is Mont Blanc or the Mont Blanc de Courmayeur (French and Italian maps disagree about the border at the summit; Wikidata gives Mont Blanc, the Factbook the Mont Blanc de Courmayeur); Serbia, because its highest point depends on whether Kosovo is counted (Wikidata's normal-rank value is Velika Rudoka in Kosovo, the Factbook gives Midžor); Monaco, whose highest point is a spot on the road Chemin des Révoires on the slope of Mont Agel, not a summit; and Vatican City, whose highest point is an unnamed spot in the Vatican Gardens on the Vatican Hill. For Denmark and the Netherlands, whose highest points overall lie outside Europe (Greenland, Saba), the cards ask for the European part; Spain's and Portugal's cards keep the country as a whole (Teide on Tenerife, Mount Pico in the Azores) and name the mainland high point in the note, as all the sources do.

## Queries

**1. Sovereign states on the continent Europe, their M49 codes and every P610 statement with rank, labels and elevation (sh <scratch>/run.sh q1, which runs: curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode "query@<scratch>/q1.rq" https://query.wikidata.org/sparql > <scratch>/q1.csv)** (Wikidata: the highest point (P610) of the sovereign states of Europe, and the English, Swedish and multilingual labels and aliases of the summits and states)

```
SELECT ?country ?countryEn ?countrySv ?m49 ?point ?pointEn ?pointSv ?pointMul ?rank ?elev WHERE {
  ?country wdt:P31 wd:Q3624078 ; wdt:P30 wd:Q46 .
  FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?country wdt:P31 wd:Q3024240 }
  OPTIONAL { ?country wdt:P2082 ?m49 }
  OPTIONAL { ?country p:P610 ?st . ?st ps:P610 ?point ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
    OPTIONAL { ?point rdfs:label ?pointEn FILTER(LANG(?pointEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?point rdfs:label ?pointSv FILTER(LANG(?pointSv) = "sv") }
    OPTIONAL { ?point rdfs:label ?pointMul FILTER(LANG(?pointMul) = "mul") }
    OPTIONAL { ?point wdt:P2044 ?elev } }
  OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countryEn FILTER(LANG(?countryEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countrySv FILTER(LANG(?countrySv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?countryEn

```

**2. P610 of Denmark (Q35) and the Netherlands (Q55) (sh <scratch>/run.sh q2, writing <scratch>/q2.csv)** (Wikidata: the highest point (P610) of the sovereign states of Europe, and the English, Swedish and multilingual labels and aliases of the summits and states)

```
SELECT ?country ?countryEn ?point ?pointEn ?rank ?elev WHERE {
  VALUES ?country { wd:Q35 wd:Q55 }
  ?country p:P610 ?st . ?st ps:P610 ?point ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
  OPTIONAL { ?point rdfs:label ?pointEn FILTER(LANG(?pointEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?point wdt:P2044 ?elev }
  OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countryEn FILTER(LANG(?countryEn) = "en") }
}

```

**3. English, Swedish and mul labels and aliases and the English and Swedish Wikipedia sitelinks of the 39 summits (sh <scratch>/run.sh q3, writing <scratch>/q3.csv)** (Wikidata: the highest point (P610) of the sovereign states of Europe, and the English, Swedish and multilingual labels and aliases of the summits and states)

```
SELECT ?point ?kind ?lang ?text WHERE {
  VALUES ?point { wd:Q912579 wd:Q62467 wd:Q3388 wd:Q921447 wd:Q322824 wd:Q837723 wd:Q209341 wd:Q3183447 wd:Q617511
    wd:Q504991 wd:Q216035 wd:Q583 wd:Q3375 wd:Q80344 wd:Q747618 wd:Q140084 wd:Q503368 wd:Q1122342 wd:Q665000
    wd:Q771431 wd:Q24457 wd:Q1850604 wd:Q47940 wd:Q2720697 wd:Q203942 wd:Q672936 wd:Q928681 wd:Q746524 wd:Q43105
    wd:Q158526 wd:Q81213 wd:Q1024 wd:Q38954 wd:Q214011 wd:Q3403 wd:Q627508 wd:Q104674 wd:Q689106 wd:Q159860 }
  { ?point rdfs:label ?text . BIND("label" AS ?kind) }
  UNION { ?point skos:altLabel ?text . BIND("alias" AS ?kind) }
  UNION { ?sl schema:about ?point ; schema:isPartOf <https://sv.wikipedia.org/> ; schema:name ?text . BIND("svwiki" AS ?kind) }
  UNION { ?sl schema:about ?point ; schema:isPartOf <https://en.wikipedia.org/> ; schema:name ?text . BIND("enwiki" AS ?kind) }
  BIND(LANG(?text) AS ?lang)
  FILTER(?kind IN ("svwiki", "enwiki") || ?lang IN ("en", "sv", "mul"))
}
ORDER BY ?point ?kind ?lang

```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 51 findings: 39 fixed, 4 rejected after checking, 8 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (198 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's summit against Wikidata P610, the Factbook's last edition and the English Wikipedia list; the Swedish names against Wikidata sv labels and the Swedish Wikipedia; national sources where these differed. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 40 cards, the 4 excluded states, the sources and the deck metadata.

Wikidata, the Factbook and the English Wikipedia name the same summit for 38 of the 40 states (the Factbook still names Kebnekaise's south peak). The two differences (Luxembourg, the Netherlands) were settled with a national source or by restricting the question; two states whose highest point differs by source (Italy, Serbia) and two without a named summit (Monaco, Vatican City) were left out. No Wikidata check was skipped; for the Netherlands the P610 check is replaced by a P17 check (method, step 9). (Round 2 later left out two label checks, Finland sv and Liechtenstein en; see method step 9.)

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 40 cards against live Wikidata, the English Wikipedia articles on the summits, Lex for Denmark and recent news for Sweden.

No card had a wrong answer. The reviewer found that the 2026 Kebnekaise measurement had been missed, that the Belgium and Denmark notes were doubtful or misleading, a missing article in the United Kingdom's English front, and "i" where Swedish uses "på" with island states and archipelagos. All were verified and fixed; the Netherlands and Iceland suggestions were applied too.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| sweden | The dossier cites the 2025 Kebnekaise measurement and says no 2026 result was found, but the Tarfala station measured the peaks on 11 September 2026 (reported 16 September 2026). | Verified: the TT report on feber.se (16 September 2026) and Stockholm University's own press release of 16 September 2026 on Mynewsdesk (south peak 2088.3 m, north peak 2096.8 m, the north peak Sweden's highest point for the eighth year in a row, since 2019; measured 11 September 2026). The su-tarfala source now is that press release; the note says "2026 measurement"; method step 4 and query 9 describe how it was found; round 0's remark was marked as superseded. The card's answer and 2,096.8 m are unchanged. | fixed |
| belgium | The note calls the site "the high point of a ridge" (from the Swedish Wikipedia only); the English Wikipedia calls it the top of a broad plateau in the High Fens. | Verified in the English article Signal de Botrange (revision 1369711733). Note reworded: "On the High Fens plateau in the Ardennes; not a distinct peak." / "På högplatån Hohes Venn i Ardennerna; ingen tydlig bergstopp." (Hohes Venn is the Wikidata Swedish label and Swedish article of the High Fens, query 15). The article was added as evidence (new verification source wikipedia-en-articles). | fixed |
| denmark | "Only centimetres higher than Yding Skovhøj and Ejer Bavnehøj" understates the 51 cm margin and leaves out that the comparison excludes the burial mound and the tower and concerns the highest natural point. | Verified against the Lex quote already in the evidence. Note now: "The highest natural point (2005 survey): 9 cm higher than Yding Skovhøj without its burial mound and 51 cm higher than Ejer Bavnehøj without its tower. …", with the Swedish to match. | fixed |
| united-kingdom | The English front "Highest point of United Kingdom" lacks the article. | Front changed to "Highest point of the United Kingdom"; method step 5 now mentions the article. | fixed |
| malta, iceland, spain, portugal | Swedish says "på" with island states and archipelagos: "Högsta punkten i Malta/Island", "i Kanarieöarna", "i Azorerna" are unidiomatic. | Fronts now "Högsta punkten på Malta" and "Högsta punkten på Island"; notes "En vulkan på Teneriffa, Kanarieöarna; …" and "På ön Pico, Azorerna; …". Method steps 5 and 7 state the exception. | fixed |
| netherlands | The P17 check would pass for Belgium or Germany as well (the Vaalserberg has three P17 values), so it confirms nothing about the card's fact. | Verified (query 13: Q159860 P17 = Q55, Q31, Q183, all normal rank). Method step 9 and the card's Wikidata evidence now say plainly that the P17 check is only a sanity check and that the normal-rank P610 value of Q55 (query 2) is the real support. | fixed |
| iceland | "by the Vatnajökull glacier" is imprecise: Öræfajökull is part of the Vatnajökull ice cap. | Verified in the English article Hvannadalshnjúkur ("on the northwestern rim of the summit crater of the Öræfajökull volcano in Vatnajökull National Park"). Note now: "On the crater rim of the Öræfajökull volcano, in Vatnajökull National Park; …" / "På kraterkanten av vulkanen Öræfajökull i Vatnajökulls nationalpark; …" (Swedish name from the Wikidata sv label, query 15). | fixed |

Language tags, metadata and most Swedish forms passed. Declined: switching all Swedish fronts to the genitive, adding a Belarusian form to the Swedish note, unifying Iceland's spelling and adding cross-language names for Portugal.

### Round 3: Licensing, attribution and documentation (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Licensing, attribution and documentation reviewer · **Scope:** Every source's licence and role, the licensing text, the method, the recorded queries, and the evidence of all 40 cards (about 23 re-fetched).

The CC0 licence and every source's licence and role were confirmed. Fixed: the account of how M49 decides the selection, missing <scratch>/ prefixes, wrong query references for Denmark and the Netherlands, duplicated P610 values for San Marino and Slovakia, unsupported or unquoted notes (Croatia, Germany), Denmark's note, Belgium's close paraphrase, the United Kingdom and Swedish "på" wording, the Gaelic label evidence, the scripts' rules and the STATEC licence description. Declined: per-card Swedish Wikipedia URLs.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| deck | The selection comes from the M49 page, labelled verification-only with UN terms forbidding derivative works, while the dossier said nothing and no selection was copied. | Verified. The un-m49 usedFor now says the selection follows M49's region Europe, and the licensing text argues why: M49 assigns every country or area of the world to one region, so a state's region is a fact of the standard (like an ISO code), not a creative choice of items, and no text or table is copied. An attempt to corroborate the membership from CC0 Wikidata (query 16, states part of the M49 subregion items) returned no rows; method step 2 records that. | fixed |
